module.name: fpctsan
module.short: Run time support and annotations for ThreadSanitizer (-fsanitize=thread)

descr.p: fpctsan is the run time part of the -fsanitize=thread compiler option (x86_64-linux, native code generator). The compiler adds the unit to every module compiled with the option: it links libtsan and contains the trampolines FPC_TSAN_READ and FPC_TSAN_WRITE that the instrumented code calls before each memory access. The trampolines preserve all general purpose registers, the flags and xmm0..xmm15.

ThreadSanitizer sees the synchronization done through the POSIX thread library (critical sections, events, thread creation and termination), but not the atomic operations of the RTL (InterlockedIncrement, InterlockedCompareExchange and others), because the RTL is not instrumented. Code that synchronizes threads only through atomic operations must be annotated with and , guarded by the FPC_SANITIZE_THREAD conditional define that the option sets.

The program must be run with address space randomization disabled (setarch $(uname -m) -R ./prog) on kernels with high mmap entropy, and compiled with debug information (-gw) to get procedure names and line numbers in the reports.
On other platforms the routines are empty.

element.name: TsanRelease
element.short: Publishes the memory accesses of the calling thread for a later TsanAcquire with the same address

descr.p: TsanRelease calls __tsan_release for aAddr. Everything the calling thread did before the call happens before everything another thread does after a later with the same address.
Call it immediately before the atomic operation that hands data over to another thread, for example before decrementing a reference count.

element.name: TsanRelease.aAddr
element.short: Address identifying the synchronization object, usually the atomic variable

element.name: TsanAcquire
element.short: Acquires the memory accesses published with TsanRelease for the same address

descr.p: TsanAcquire calls __tsan_acquire for aAddr. Call it immediately after the atomic operation that observed the hand-over, for example when a reference count dropped to zero and the shared object is about to be freed.

element.name: TsanAcquire.aAddr
element.short: Address passed to TsanRelease by the publishing thread
